sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/0baeccd234670e36df4c7f969b488732]

The atmospheric pressure [MATH: P,] in kilopascals, [MATH: h] kilometers above sea level can be modeled using the exponential function [MATH: P(h) = ab^h,] where [MATH: a] and [MATH: b] are constants. According to this model, what is the atmospheric pressure at [MATH: 4] kilometers above sea level? Express your answer to the nearest in kilopascal.

sections.normalized_html:
Notice that the following points lie on the graph:

[MATH: (0,100), \quad (1, 90), \quad (2,81)]

Using these points, we note that there is a common ratio of [MATH: 0.9] between successive values of [MATH: P] for integer [MATH: t\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: \dfrac{90}{100} = \dfrac{81}{90} = 0.9]

Therefore, we must have [MATH: b = 0.9.] Hence,

[MATH: P(h) = a\cdot 0.9^h.]

In addition, [MATH: P(0) = 100.] Therefore, [MATH: a=100,] and we have

[MATH: P(h) = 100 \cdot 0.9^h.]

Finally, to determine the atmospheric pressure at [MATH: 4] kilometers above sea level, we evaluate [MATH: P(4)\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: P(4) = 100 \cdot 0.9^4 \approx 66\,\textrm{kPa}]

rounded to the nearest kilopascal.
